tasks.title: Essay: Exchange visit priorities
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write 140–190 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: In your English class you have been discussing how to plan a successful college exchange visit. Now your English teacher has asked you to write an essay.
Write an essay using all the notes and giving reasons for your point of view.

tasks.title: Review: Exchange welcome pack
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 140–190 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.heading: Reviews wanted
paragraphs: Have you used the welcome pack our college gives to exchange visitors?
Write a review of the welcome pack for the college website. Describe what it contains, say how helpful it was for you, and recommend one improvement.
The best reviews will be published on our website.

tasks.title: Article: Making exchange students feel welcome
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 140–190 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.heading: Articles wanted
paragraphs: Our college is planning a new exchange programme and wants ideas to make visiting students feel welcome.
Write an article for the programme coordinator suggesting one practical way to help exchange students settle in, explaining why it would work and what the benefits would be.
We will share the best ideas with the planning team.

tasks.title: Email: Exchange visit arrangements
tasks.instruction: Answer one of these questions. Write 140–190 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.subject: Exchange visit next month
paragraphs: I am writing to confirm the exchange visit from your college next month. We are very excited to welcome your group!
Could you please let me know if you prefer to stay with a host family or in a student residence? Also, what type of activities would you like us to arrange for your free time?
Finally, do you have any dietary requirements or special needs we should know about?
I look forward to hearing from you.

promptBlocks.text: Write your email to Ms. Rossi. You should explain your preferences, suggest one activity, and ask a question about the schedule.

designReview.specificSetting: a college exchange partnership planning brief 1

tasks.scenario: Essay about priorities for planning a successful college exchange visit
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Scenario is original; focuses on exchange planning, not generic life skills or environment. Notes are specific to exchange context. No overlap with existing test fingerprints.

tasks.scenario: Review of a welcome pack for exchange visitors
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Review of a welcome pack is a novel scenario; not a book, film, or facility review. No overlap with existing reviews.

tasks.scenario: Article suggesting a practical way to help exchange students settle in
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Article focuses on welcoming exchange students; not a generic 'learning beyond lessons' or 'skills' article. Specific to exchange context.

tasks.scenario: Email replying to exchange coordinator about accommodation, activities, and dietary needs
tasks.purpose: explain a position and request arrangements
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Email is a reply to an exchange coordinator about visit details; not a friend email about weekend plans or course advice. Unique scenario.

designReview.centralTension: access and convenience versus long-term responsibility in school exchange visits
designReview.overallOriginalityCheck: All tasks are built around the specific setting of a college exchange partnership planning brief. No reused scenarios, audiences, or content points from previous tests. Forbidden concepts (e.g., peer learning, environment, digital communication) are avoided. Each task has a concrete audience and clear communicative purpose. The design is original and level-appropriate.
